newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway to host anti-personnel mines meeting.
newsitem.headline: Norway to host anti-personnel mines meeting.

text.p: Norway said on Monday it would host a major conference on anti-personnel mines in September in an effort to forge an international accord banning the weapons.
"The use of anti-personnel mines against civilians is one of the biggest humanitarian problems today," Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal said in a statement issued by his ministry.
He called for a total ban on their use as soon as possible.

Norway is part of a core group of 11 nations pushing for such a ban. The point of the Oslo meeting is to draw up a draft text for an accord that could be signed in Ottawa, Canada, before the end of the year, the foreign ministry said.
It said the conference was expected to draw delegates from more than 100 countries and last for two weeks.
A conference was held in February in Vienna as part of the so-called "Ottawa process" begun last October at a 50-nation forum hosted by Canada.
Major mine producers such as the United States, Britain and France attended and India, Pakistan, Russia and Ukraine were present as observers. China declined to attend.
The conference demonstrated many governments would be prepared to sign a ban treaty by the end of the year, according to the International Campaign to Ban Landmines (ICBL).
Over 100 million landmines lie buried in 64 countries around the world. According to U.N. statistics they kill or maim one person every 20 minutes, or 25,000 people a year.
